tagline: Down the barrier islands from the Isle of Eight Flags.
intro: A1A starts in Fernandina Beach on Amelia Island, just below the Georgia line, and runs south along the barrier islands, over the Nassau River into Duval County and across the St. Johns by ferry to the fishing village of Mayport. From there it passes through Atlantic Beach, Neptune Beach and Jacksonville Beach and ends at the St. Johns County line, about 40 miles down.

Fernandina counts eight flags flown over its island, two of them belonging to a Republic of East Florida and a Republic of the Floridas. The Spanish laid the town out in 1811, the last one platted under the Laws of the Indies in the Western Hemisphere.

moments.title: American Beach
moments.text: Abraham Lincoln Lewis, Florida's first Black millionaire, founded this beach town in 1935 for African Americans shut out of other beaches, offering "Recreation and Relaxation Without Humiliation."

moments.title: Fort George Island
moments.text: On an island holding the highest ground on the Atlantic coast south of New Jersey, the oyster shells of Timucua mounds were burned into tabby for the slave quarters of Kingsley Plantation.

moments.title: Mayport Ferry
moments.text: A ferry has carried traffic across the St. Johns here since 1874, a 0.9-mile crossing that saves the 28-mile drive around by the Dames Point Bridge.
